title: SNMP TRAP/INFORM Receiver Driver Configuration
description: Per-driver-type schema for `type: snmp_trap_receiver` entries (FR-SB-006; Sprint C8, XEDGE-484; CRD §4.6). Listens for inbound TRAP/INFORM notifications and maps each one's varbind OIDs to tags -- event-driven, not polled, the same shape as xedge.drivers.mqtt_subscriber (push-based southbound data, confirmed against pysnmp's own real notification-receiver mechanism before writing this, not assumed). tag_groups.scan_rate_ms does not apply here (there is nothing to poll) and is intentionally absent from this schema.

host.description: This instance's own bind address -- it is listening for inbound notifications, not connecting out to a device, unlike every other driver's `host` field.

version.description: Which security model this instance accepts inbound notifications under. Unlike the snmp_client manager driver, this is the *receiving* side's own accepted credentials, checked against whatever the sending device presents.

community.description: Required for version v1/v2c: the community string an inbound TRAP/INFORM must carry to be accepted.

v3_priv_protocol.description: Requires v3_auth_protocol != 'none', same RFC 3414 rule as the snmp_client manager driver's identical field.

trap_oid.description: Numeric dotted OID of the varbind this tag reads from an inbound notification's payload, e.g. a vendor-specific OID from the sending device's own MIB. A notification is typically several varbinds at once (see xedge.core.snmp_notify's own sysUpTime.0/snmpTrapOID.0 example) -- each configured tag independently picks out the one varbind whose OID matches, from whichever notification arrives; varbinds with no matching tag are logged and dropped, not an error.

scaling.description: FR-DP-003: engineering_value = raw * scale + offset. Ignored for a non-numeric varbind value.
